_comment: Single source of truth for malicious npm packages tracked by PoisonChain. category: 'compromised_legitimate' = legitimate package whose specific versions were hijacked; 'malicious_intent' = package was malicious from the start (typosquat etc.). datadog_added: earliest date the package appeared in the Datadog dataset (ZIP filename prefix). version_dates: {version: 'YYYY-MM-DD'} maps each version to its Datadog discovery date. For Nexus/lockfile scans, malicious_intent packages are inherently dangerous by name, while compromised_legitimate packages are only dangerous at specific listed versions.

categories.compromised_legitimate: Legitimate npm package whose maintainer account was hijacked. Only specific versions are malicious; the package name itself remains in use.
categories.malicious_intent: Package published with malicious intent (typosquat, supply chain pretense). Any version of the package is a sign of compromise.

datadog_auto.name: Datadog malicious-software-packages-dataset (auto-imported)
datadog_auto.notes: Synced daily by .github/workflows/refresh-malicious-packages.yml. This campaign's entries are authoritative-refreshed; do not edit by hand.
